analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. I examined two files.

1. changelog.d/coordinator-traffic-verdict.md (new, head lines 1-5) describes three things:
- A new `Traffic:` line in status and a new doctor check.
- A `coordinator_connection` field in the daemon state file.
- Automatic re-registration of unauthorized connections. The first attempt comes after a random 15-30 min delay, then at 30 min, 1 h, 2 h and every 4 h. It is gated on the provider being idle.

2. docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines 998-1009, plus the date at line 3) documents the Traffic line. Its sources are ServingReadiness.swift and StatusCommand+Traffic.swift.

No source code is in this batch, so neither file is evidence of a regression.

Security-relevant questions for the integration pass:

(a) Re-registration and TB-011/T-053. A re-registration starts a new coordinator verification session. Check that the provider-side reregister path:
- invalidates prior App Attest grant/lease state;
- rejects or cancels queued work bound to the old connection;
- does not reuse stale proofs. Under protocol 1, it must show a fresh socket nonce and endpoint custody.

(b) Idle gating and T-010/A-001. Confirm the idle check (accepted/local requests, loads, Autopilot, drain, update) is race-free. Otherwise an in-flight request could be torn down or orphaned mid-stream.

(c) State-file contents and A-008/T-058. The state file must not contain tokens, stable identities or raw coordinator diagnostics beyond the documented fields. Confirm the file stays owner-only.

(d) Diagnostic trust boundary. The coordinator-provided reason text is displayed locally. It should be treated as diagnostic only, not as an authorization signal (T-052). Escaping or sanitization of terminal output is worth a check.

(e) Coordinator load from the backoff schedule is bounded by design. Verify the jitter and backoff in code.

Threat model gap: TB-011/T-053 may need a note that the provider now initiates periodic re-registration while unauthorized. This is pending source review.
